title: Sowing radish microgreens
subtitle: How to fill, sow, and start the blackout phase for a radish microgreen tray
excerpt: Sowing radish microgreens takes about five minutes. Fill a 25 cm tray with pre-dampened seed compost, scatter radish seed at 20 to 25 g per tray, press into contact with the medium, then cover for the blackout phase. Cotyledons emerge in two to three days.
sourceNotes: UMass Extension microgreens guides (open-access). Cornell Cooperative Extension indoor growing material. Standard microgreen-growing practice synthesised from extension service material.

glossaryTerms.definition: A fine-textured, low-fertility growing medium designed for germination. Seed compost has smaller particles than multi-purpose compost, which helps seeds make even contact with the medium surface. Use it for microgreen trays rather than multi-purpose compost.

The period immediately after sowing when a second tray is stacked on top, blocking light from the sown tray. In darkness, germinating seeds direct energy into pushing the shoot upward rather than greening. The shoots reach 2 to 3 cm before the cover is removed and the tray is moved to light.

content.text: Radish is one of the easiest microgreen crops to sow: large seed, fast germination, no pre-treatment required. The sowing process takes about five minutes. What follows covers the steps from empty tray to the start of the blackout phase.

One 25 cm × 25 cm growing tray (with drainage holes or without, both work). One second tray of the same size for the blackout cover. Seed compost. A watering can or jug. Radish seed: 20 to 25 g per tray. A flat tool or piece of card for pressing.

Step 1: pre-dampen the compost. Add water to the seed compost before filling the tray, mixing until it holds together when squeezed but does not drip. Starting with damp medium is better than watering after filling; it avoids washing the seed off the surface.
Step 2: fill the tray. Pack the pre-dampened compost into the tray to within 1 to 2 cm of the rim. Level the surface with a straight edge or the flat of your hand.
is better than multi-purpose compost. The finer texture helps seeds make good contact with the surface, giving more even germination.
Step 3: scatter the seed. Weigh out 20 to 25 g of radish seed and scatter evenly across the surface from 10 to 15 cm above the tray. Work in rows or small sections to avoid piling seed in one area.

Step 4: press. Place a flat piece of card or the base of a second tray on top of the seed and press down firmly. Radish seeds are large enough to be pressed into good contact with the medium with one firm pass.

: stack the second tray directly on top of the sown tray. Add a light weight (a filled water glass or small tin) on top. Place in any dark or dim location at room temperature. No further action is needed for two to three days.

attrs.heading: Troubleshooting
attrs.intro: Common sowing-stage problems with radish microgreens.

items.symptom: Seed clusters in some spots and bare patches in others
items.fix: Scatter from higher up (20 to 25 cm) to help seed spread. Work systematically across the tray in small strips. A consistent spreading motion prevents piling.

items.symptom: Medium floods and seed washes to edges when watered after sowing
items.cause: Watering after sowing rather than pre-dampening the medium.
items.fix: Pre-dampen the compost before filling the tray on the next attempt. If you need to water after sowing, water from below by setting the tray in a shallow outer tray of water.

items.symptom: Seeds not germinating after three days
items.cause: Seed not in contact with the medium, or room too cold.
items.fix: Press the seed more firmly on the next attempt. Confirm room temperature is above 15°C.
